answer: Orchard-edge routing weight. Each agent’s routing score is the count of distinct neighbor clusters reaching it, weighted by latency variance across those paths. A new identity starts with one edge and near-zero weight, so traffic barely routes through it until independent clusters connect. An attacker must operate many geographically dispersed clusters with sustained, low-variance links—a voyage of months per cluster, each costing real bandwidth and hosting. A single glacier-slow or unstable link drops the score. Cost scales with distinct infrastructure, not registrations.
